input.quote: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
input.rationale: Article II §IV(b) binds Licensee (our client) to permit audits of its accounting records. The clause satisfies parts of the playbook position — the auditor must be an independent CPA/audit professional selected by mutual agreement, and p0064 already allocates audit cost to Licensor unless a discrepancy exceeding 5% is found — but it contains no frequency cap (audits could be demanded repeatedly), gives no advance notice (the 30-day period is our compliance deadline after a request, not prior notice), and does not limit the audit to business hours, bind the auditor to confidentiality, or confine the review to records provided off-site. Redline inserts once-per-12-months, 30 days' prior written notice, business hours, auditor confidentiality, and no access to our systems or facilities; cost allocation is left as-is since it already meets the preferred 5% threshold.

ops.oldText: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
ops.newText: Any such audit shall be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice from Licensor, during Licensee's normal business hours, and by an auditor bound by written obligations of confidentiality no less protective than those set forth in this Agreement. Any such audit shall be limited to the accounting records described above, which Licensee may make available off-site, and shall not include access to Licensee's systems, networks or facilities.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have limited the records audit to once every twelve months, on thirty days' prior written notice, during business hours and by an auditor under confidentiality, and confirmed the review is of records only rather than our systems. As drafted the right was unlimited in frequency and gave us no advance notice; if helpful we can accept annual audits on fifteen days' notice as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Cap audit at once per 12 months with 30 days' notice, business hours, confidentiality-bound auditor and no system access.
